claims.text: The as-deposited FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers have minimal pre-existing short-range order.
Controlled low-temperature annealing at approximately 0.3–0.4 Tm can enhance short-range order in the BCC layers.
Annealing at approximately 0.3–0.4 Tm is below the onset of grain growth for the proposed multilayers.
The proposed annealing treatment can selectively enhance SRO while retaining the nanoscale multilayer architecture.
Increased SRO produces an additional barrier to dislocation motion in the BCC layers.
Enhanced SRO raises local lattice friction.
Higher local lattice friction hinders dislocation nucleation.
Higher local lattice friction hinders dislocation glide.
Hindered dislocation motion delays the onset of plastic flow under sustained loading.
The proposed modulation of dislocation dynamics produces a more uniform strain distribution across the multilayer.
Annealed multilayers will have greater creep resistance than as-deposited multilayers tested under identical conditions.
Annealed multilayers will exhibit a delayed onset of plastic deformation relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed multilayers will exhibit a more uniform strain distribution between FCC and BCC layers.
High-resolution TEM and atom probe tomography will reveal enhanced SRO correlated with improved mechanical performance.
The qualitative link between enhanced SRO and improved creep resistance is supported.
